list.name: dataset
list.label: Report family
list.definition: report families present in the serving table
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT dataset FROM board_positioning ORDER BY dataset

list.name: market
list.label: Market
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT market_label AS __text, market_code AS __value FROM board_positioning WHERE dataset='$dataset' ORDER BY __text

list.name: group
list.label: Cohort
list.definition: cohort groups for this family, by reader-facing name
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT cohort_label AS __text, cohort_group AS __value FROM board_positioning WHERE dataset='$dataset' ORDER BY __text

panels.title: Latest reading — ${market:text} · ${group:text}
panels.description: The newest row for this market and cohort, regardless of the time picker -- the Report date tile is what makes that honest. The percentile is CAUSAL: each week is ranked only against weeks at or before itself, computed in pandas and never in SQL. It is blank where the pool is under 140 weeks, because a rank off a short history renders exactly as confidently as one off twenty years. Open interest and its percentile are market-level, identical on every cohort row, so they live in their own panels rather than being printed here as if they described this cohort.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT report_date AS 'Report date', share AS '% of open interest', CASE WHEN n_pool >= 140 THEN share_pctile END AS 'Percentile of own history', chg_2w AS '2-week change (pp)' FROM board_positioning WHERE dataset='$dataset' AND market_code='$market' AND cohort_group='$group' ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 1
targets.queryText: SELECT report_date AS 'Report date', share AS '% of open interest', CASE WHEN n_pool >= 140 THEN share_pctile END AS 'Percentile of own history', chg_2w AS '2-week change (pp)' FROM board_positioning WHERE dataset='$dataset' AND market_code='$market' AND cohort_group='$group' ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: Asset managers vs hedge funds vs their total — ${market:text}
panels.description: All three on ONE axis because all three are the same quantity: net position as a percent of open interest. 'Speculative total' is the EXACT SUM of the two components on the financial-futures family, so it is drawn unfilled and never stacked -- stacking a part with its own total draws twice the real exposure. On the commodity and legacy families the two components do not exist and the total falls back to managed money / non-commercial, so the panel degrades to an honest single line rather than going blank. No percentile here: the combined cohort's percentile is not bounded by its components'.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT ts/1000 AS time, MAX(CASE WHEN cohort_group='asset_mgr' THEN share END) AS 'Asset managers', MAX(CASE WHEN cohort_group='lev_money' THEN share END) AS 'Hedge funds', MAX(CASE WHEN cohort_group IN ('asset_mgr+lev_money','m_money','noncomm') THEN share END) AS 'Speculative total' FROM board_positioning WHERE dataset='$dataset' AND market_code='$market' AND ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to GROUP BY ts ORDER BY ts
targets.queryText: SELECT ts/1000 AS time, MAX(CASE WHEN cohort_group='asset_mgr' THEN share END) AS 'Asset managers', MAX(CASE WHEN cohort_group='lev_money' THEN share END) AS 'Hedge funds', MAX(CASE WHEN cohort_group IN ('asset_mgr+lev_money','m_money','noncomm') THEN share END) AS 'Speculative total' FROM board_positioning WHERE dataset='$dataset' AND market_code='$market' AND ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to GROUP BY ts ORDER BY ts

panels.title: Net position as % of open interest — ${group:text}
panels.description: The cohort the dropdown selects, which is the only share chart that works for EVERY cohort on every family -- dealers, producers, swap dealers included. Coloured by SIGN rather than by identity: the entity here changes with the dropdown, so there is no entity for a colour to follow, and a signed quantity straddling zero is the diverging case. Red below zero (net short), blue above (net long); those two hues are deliberately outside the cohort palette above so no colour means two things on this board.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT ts/1000 AS time, share AS '% of open interest' FROM board_positioning WHERE dataset='$dataset' AND market_code='$market' AND cohort_group='$group' AND ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to ORDER BY ts
targets.queryText: SELECT ts/1000 AS time, share AS '% of open interest' FROM board_positioning WHERE dataset='$dataset' AND market_code='$market' AND cohort_group='$group' AND ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to ORDER BY ts

panels.title: Percentiles of own history — ${group:text}
panels.description: The repo's distinguishing asset as a HISTORY rather than one number. Both series are 0-100 so one axis is honest. Every point ranks its week against weeks at or before itself only; the ranks are precomputed in pandas because the segment boundaries a rank must respect come from a regex over free-text contract units. The share percentile is the COHORT's and is blank under 140 weeks of pool; the open-interest percentile is the MARKET's and is ranked only within the current contract-unit segment, so n_pool describes the first and not the second. Dashed lines mark the 10th and 90th.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT ts/1000 AS time, CASE WHEN n_pool >= 140 THEN share_pctile END AS 'Share percentile (cohort)', oi_pctile AS 'Open interest percentile (market)' FROM board_positioning WHERE dataset='$dataset' AND market_code='$market' AND cohort_group='$group' AND ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to ORDER BY ts
targets.queryText: SELECT ts/1000 AS time, CASE WHEN n_pool >= 140 THEN share_pctile END AS 'Share percentile (cohort)', oi_pctile AS 'Open interest percentile (market)' FROM board_positioning WHERE dataset='$dataset' AND market_code='$market' AND cohort_group='$group' AND ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to ORDER BY ts

panels.title: Open interest (contracts)
panels.description: A MARKET-week quantity, identical on every cohort row, so it is not filtered by the cohort dropdown and does not pretend to be per-cohort. MAX over the week's rows, never SUM: summing across cohort rows yields a plausible number three to six times too large. Contracts, not notional -- so it is not comparable across contract sizes, which is why full-size and micro bitcoin are separate markets here rather than one line.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT ts/1000 AS time, MAX(open_interest) AS 'open interest' FROM board_positioning WHERE dataset='$dataset' AND market_code='$market' AND ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to GROUP BY ts ORDER BY ts
targets.queryText: SELECT ts/1000 AS time, MAX(open_interest) AS 'open interest' FROM board_positioning WHERE dataset='$dataset' AND market_code='$market' AND ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to GROUP BY ts ORDER BY ts

panels.title: Price — ${market:text}
panels.description: A PROXY, never the reported contract -- lib/pricemap names the gap per entry, and the worst case is VIX, where positioning is in futures while this price is spot. Sampled as-of each report Tuesday, strictly backward and capped at 10 days of staleness, so a dead symbol leaves a gap instead of a flat line. Its own panel rather than an overlay on positioning: price and percent-of-open-interest are different scales, and a second y-axis is the one chart mistake this board will not make. Blank for most commodity and legacy markets, which have no mapped symbol.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT ts/1000 AS time, MAX(price) AS 'price' FROM board_positioning WHERE dataset='$dataset' AND market_code='$market' AND ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to GROUP BY ts ORDER BY ts
targets.queryText: SELECT ts/1000 AS time, MAX(price) AS 'price' FROM board_positioning WHERE dataset='$dataset' AND market_code='$market' AND ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to GROUP BY ts ORDER BY ts

defaults.noValue: no mapped price for this market

panels.title: Latest week, every cohort — ${market:text}
panels.description: The numeric answer to 'show them separately' for every cohort at once, on all three families. Combined rows sort last and are flagged, because a combined row is the sum of rows above it and summing the column would double-count. Open interest and its percentile are excluded on purpose: they are market-level, and printing them on six rows invites reading six measurements where there is one.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT cohort_label AS 'cohort', share AS '% of OI', CASE WHEN n_pool >= 140 THEN share_pctile END AS 'percentile', chg_2w AS '2w change (pp)', net AS 'net contracts', n_pool AS 'weeks ranked against', TRIM((CASE WHEN cohort_group LIKE '%+%' THEN 'sum of its components ' ELSE '' END) || (CASE WHEN n_pool < 140 THEN 'short history' ELSE '' END)) AS 'note' FROM board_positioning WHERE dataset='$dataset' AND market_code='$market' AND ts = (SELECT MAX(ts) FROM board_positioning WHERE dataset='$dataset' AND market_code='$market') ORDER BY (cohort_group LIKE '%+%'), ABS(share) DESC
targets.queryText: SELECT cohort_label AS 'cohort', share AS '% of OI', CASE WHEN n_pool >= 140 THEN share_pctile END AS 'percentile', chg_2w AS '2w change (pp)', net AS 'net contracts', n_pool AS 'weeks ranked against', TRIM((CASE WHEN cohort_group LIKE '%+%' THEN 'sum of its components ' ELSE '' END) || (CASE WHEN n_pool < 140 THEN 'short history' ELSE '' END)) AS 'note' FROM board_positioning WHERE dataset='$dataset' AND market_code='$market' AND ts = (SELECT MAX(ts) FROM board_positioning WHERE dataset='$dataset' AND market_code='$market') ORDER BY (cohort_group LIKE '%+%'), ABS(share) DESC
